sections.approach: A second delivery kind, listen. 'session_listen {workspace, wait}' is a long poll (the canvas_changes pattern, wait capped at MAX_WAIT_MS): it returns the next sling queued for the workspace's agent, or none. A sling with no profile goes to the agent's queue when a listener is attached (waiting, seen in the last seconds, or working on a sling it took) or when no process runs; otherwise to the process as today. A sling that names a profile goes only to a process, as today. The queued sling is the same message as text: the packet's images are written to the packet directory (the canvas_read pattern, at=<dir> in the header), line 1 names the agent, and the note tells a listener to pass --agent and set its status. Taking a sling sets the agent working. A reply that cannot be written puts the sling back. The pure state (queue, attached, the message text) lives in the core; the daemon holds it behind a mutex and condvar; the CLI loops the poll until a sling comes, prints it and exits, so a background shell wakes the session. The plugin gets a /slinger-listen command. The app shows a queued sling with nobody listening.

sections.context: The owner wants to read and mark up PDFs with the pen, cut sections out of them onto thinking canvases, and sling marked-up pages to an agent that sees both the ink and the page under it. Slinger has no PDF or image support today: SPEC section 4 and docs/design/canvas-file.md list images as not in v1, so this starts with a spec change.
sections.approach: A PDF is not a new pane or document type. It is one new canvas item kind `pdf` (frame, hash: the PDF's blob id, page, optional crop in PDF points). An opened PDF is a canvas of these items stacked top to bottom on one canvas page, with ordinary ink over it, so pen, lasso, undo, pages, sling and packets work unchanged. A snippet is the same item with a crop, copied through the existing clipboard path onto any canvas: vector-sharp, linked to its source, no pixel blobs. The PDF's bytes go into the record as a blob. The core treats the PDF as opaque and never parses it. Only the macOS app can draw a PDF (PDFKit / CoreGraphics; slingerd also ships for Linux), so the app draws pages in platform/pdf.rs and, at sling time, renders the PDF under the slung ink and extracts the words in those regions; the packet carries crops of the ink over the page plus a line of the exact words per cluster. The core's render draws ink over a supplied backdrop, which needs a small PNG decoder (miniz_oxide is already a dependency). A canvas made from a PDF opens in reader mode: locked vertical scroll and fit to the pane's width, nothing else. Open design point for the note (B6): clustering happens in the daemon, so the app does not know which regions a sling needs. Lean: the app sends each PDF page the selection touches at packet scale and the daemon crops (one request). Alternative: the app asks the daemon for the regions first, then renders only those (fewer pixels, a new verb).

sections.context: slinger.app installs to /Applications, but it never starts slingerd and the repo ships nothing that does. Until someone runs slingerd from a shell the window is dead and tells a GUI user to type `slingerd --socket /var/folders/...`. A daemon not started from a login shell cannot find Claude Code (`--claude` is a bare name looked up on PATH) and has no log (stderr is its only channel). A closed terminal kills it (SIGHUP is not handled). `bundle.sh --install` copies the binaries to two places, and after an update the old daemon keeps running with nothing to say so: the protocol carries one integer version and no build. The bundle has no icon. Source: the 2026-11-20 audit (slinger-558786), checked against the code. Owner decisions: slingerd outlives the app; the app starts the bundled slingerd when none answers; one install location (binaries inside the .app, CLI symlinked into ~/.local/bin); a login item (SMAppService) is later.
sections.approach: Make 'a daemon is there' something the bundled app guarantees, so the error stops existing for its user. Daemon first, so that a daemon nobody started from a shell works: a log file and SIGHUP ignored (step 1), Claude Code found from fixed places without a login shell (step 2). Then identity: one build stamp in slinger-control that every binary carries (step 3) and two verbs, daemon_info and daemon_stop, with CLI commands (step 4). Then the bundle holds all three binaries and --install links the CLI into it (step 5). Then the app: a pure state machine (crates/app/src/launch.rs) decides, a small backend thread connects and spawns, the scene shows 'Starting slingerd…' (step 6); on a build that differs the app offers 'Restart slingerd', which is daemon_stop followed by the same start loop (step 7). Icon (step 8) and the docs' single install path (step 9) close it. Rules kept: the app stays a client of the socket and never links the core; decisions live in pure modules with tests and platform/ gets no new code; only a bundled app with no `[daemon] socket` in its config starts a daemon, so a bare slinger-app (tests, cargo run, other worktrees) never touches the user's record; the daemon's locks (socket and data directory, exit 4) make a double start harmless; a restart is always asked, never automatic, because it ends running agents. Each step updates the contract docs it changes and leaves main green on `cargo xtask check-all`; what only a person can see is a line in docs/hand-check.md named in the step. Step descriptions are in each step's `description` field of the plan file.

steps.title: daemon: --log <FILE> for slingerd's and its agents' stderr; SIGHUP no longer ends it
steps.description:
Why: a slingerd nobody started from a terminal has nowhere to write (its stderr is its only log: lib.rs:148, canvases.rs warnings; agents inherit it, processes.rs:208-209), and it traps only SIGTERM and SIGINT (crates/daemon/src/lib.rs:215), so a closed terminal kills it.
Add:
- Flag `--log <PATH>` on slingerd (crates/daemon/src/lib.rs Args). With it, before serving: make the parent directory; if the file is over 1 MiB rename it to `<PATH>.1` (replacing the old one); open it for append; point fd 2 at it (rustix, already a dependency; safe API such as rustix::stdio::dup2_stderr), so the daemon's warnings and every agent's stderr land there. Without the flag nothing changes (stderr as today).
- With --log only, one line at start: `<local time> slingerd <version> (<build>) pid <pid>: serving <data dir> on <socket>`, and one at a clean stop. The "says nothing on success" contract on a terminal stays.
- SIGHUP is ignored (signal-hook: register it so the default action is replaced). SIGTERM and SIGINT stop as today.
Constraints: the fd redirect must happen only in the slingerd binary (crates/daemon/src/main.rs), never inside `daemon::run` when tests call it in-process (it would redirect the test runner's stderr): e.g. main asks the library for the parsed log path, or passes a hook. Put the code in a new crates/daemon/src/log.rs; the pure parts (rotate-or-not by size, the line format) are functions with unit tests. No unsafe (layer rule platform-owns-ffi).
Tests: unit tests in log.rs; crates/daemon/tests/stderr.rs or signals.rs (they run the real binary, with its own --socket, a --data-dir in a tempdir and --scratch): with --log, a stand-in claude that writes to stderr shows up in the file, and so does a "workspace not loaded" warning; a file over the limit is rotated at start; after SIGHUP the daemon still answers, then SIGTERM exits 0.
Docs in the same commit: docs/service.md "The daemon" (synopsis, the flag, SIGHUP), ARCHITECTURE.md "Inside the daemon", CHANGELOG under Unreleased.

steps.title: daemon: find Claude Code without PATH when --claude is not given
steps.description:
Why: `--claude` defaults to the bare name `claude` (crates/daemon/src/lib.rs:78, store.rs:60), looked up on the daemon's PATH at spawn (processes.rs:194). A slingerd started by the app gets launchd's PATH (/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin); Claude Code is usually in ~/.local/bin. The first sling then fails with "install Claude Code, or pass its path with 'slingerd --claude <PATH>'" (processes.rs:82-84). No login shell is to be run for this (owner decision).
Add (new file crates/daemon/src/processes/program.rs; processes.rs is 445 lines, do not grow it past 500):
- `--claude` becomes optional. Given: used as written, as today. Not given: at each session start (not once at startup, so an install made later is found) take the first of these that is an executable file: `claude` in each folder of the daemon's PATH, then ~/.local/bin/claude, ~/.claude/local/claude, /opt/homebrew/bin/claude, /usr/local/bin/claude, ~/.nix-profile/bin/claude, /etc/profiles/per-user/<user>/bin/claude. Keep the list in one const.
- Pure functions with unit tests: `candidates(path: Option<&OsStr>, home: Option<&Path>, user: Option<&str>) -> Vec<PathBuf>` (order, empty PATH entries dropped, no HOME) and the pick over an injected "is executable" check. The environment is read once in `run` and passed in as a value: tests must not set process environment variables (they run in parallel).
- None found: a typed error, code `not_found`, message naming that Claude Code was not found and the places searched, hint "install Claude Code, or start slingerd with --claude <PATH>".
- `Processes` exposes the path it would run now (`Option<PathBuf>`), for the daemon_info verb of a later step.
Tests: unit tests above; crates/daemon/src/tests/process.rs through a real socket: with a search whose PATH lacks claude and whose home holds .local/bin/claude (the stand-in script the tests already write), a session starts; with none, session start fails `not_found` with the hint; an explicit --claude still wins.
Docs in the same commit: docs/service.md "The daemon" (--claude default) and "Sessions" where it names the program; ARCHITECTURE.md "Inside the daemon"; CHANGELOG.
Hand check (one line in docs/hand-check.md, under a heading "## Launcher (plan <this plan id>)", not a step): from a slingerd started by the bundled app, start an agent and sling once: Claude Code is found, its hooks report, its Bash tool finds git/cargo/sd, its MCP servers load (the agent inherits launchd's short PATH).

steps.title: control: one build stamp that the daemon, the CLI and the app all carry
steps.description:
Why: only slingerd is stamped with its commit (crates/daemon/build.rs sets SLINGER_BUILD_SHA and SLINGER_BUILD_DIRTY; used in crates/daemon/src/feedback.rs:66 through slinger_core::feedback::build, crates/core/src/feedback.rs:225). The app must compare its own build with the daemon's, and it may not link the core (layer rule app-uses-the-socket). Every binary links slinger-control.
Do:
- Move crates/daemon/build.rs to crates/control/build.rs unchanged in behaviour (a value already in the environment wins; no git: nothing set; the rerun-if-changed list; the `../..` root still holds from crates/control). Remove the daemon's build script.
- New crates/control/src/build.rs: `pub fn stamp() -> String` (the sha in lowercase, `-dirty` after it, `dev` with no sha: exactly today's text) over a pure `text(sha: Option<&str>, dirty: Option<&str>)`, and `pub const PACKAGE: &str = env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")`. Move the formatter and its tests out of crates/core/src/feedback.rs; the daemon's feedback.rs calls control's. Do not name anything `VERSION`: control already exports the protocol's `VERSION`.
- Leave `SLINGER_BUILD_SOURCE` and `feedback::default_file` (crates/daemon/src/feedback.rs:16-19, 139-143) as they are.
- crates/control/src/lib.rs is 477 lines: add only the `mod` and the `pub use`.
Behaviour that must not change: the `build` field of feedback notes; `slinger --version` and `slingerd --version` print the package version.
Tests: the moved unit tests in control; crates/daemon/tests/feedback.rs and crates/daemon/src/tests/feedback.rs still pass untouched (they hold the note's build text).
Docs in the same commit: ARCHITECTURE.md lines about build.rs and SLINGER_BUILD_SHA (around 347-348) and the layer text of crates/control.
Known limit, to state in the doc comment: two builds from the same commit with different uncommitted changes carry the same stamp.

steps.title: verbs daemon_info and daemon_stop: control, daemon, and `slinger daemon info|stop`
steps.description:
Why: the protocol has one integer VERSION (crates/control/src/wire.rs:11) and no request says which build answers, so an updated app cannot tell that an old daemon still runs; and the only way to stop a daemon is to find its pid.
Follow "Adding a verb" in docs/service.md. Step 1 there (the core) does not apply: these verbs describe the daemon's process, which the core cannot know (core-is-pure forbids std::env and std::process). Say so in the commit message.
- control: new crates/control/src/daemon.rs. `DaemonAsk` tagged by `op` (`daemon_info`, `daemon_stop`), read through one `Request::Daemon` variant marked `#[serde(untagged, skip_serializing)]` as crates/control/src/session.rs does, with the test that the ask writes the line `Request` reads. Replies: `DaemonInfo { version, build, protocol, pid, started_ms, exe, socket, data_dir, claude: Option<String>, slinger, log: Option<String> }` (version = build::PACKAGE, build = build::stamp(), claude = the path it would run now or null, log = the --log path or null) and `DaemonStopped { pid }`. Typed `Client::daemon_info()` and `Client::daemon_stop()`. lib.rs is 477 lines: add only the mod, the pub use and the two variants; move something out by concept if it would pass 500.
- daemon: new crates/daemon/src/server/daemon.rs and one arm in `answer` (crates/daemon/src/server.rs, 474 lines). `daemon_stop` replies, then stops exactly as SIGTERM does (`Stopper::stop`: replies already owed still go out, agents end, socket file and socket name removed, exit 0). The handler needs the Stopper and the facts `serve` knows (log path, start time): carry them on the Store or pass them to `converse`; no globals.
- CLI: new crates/cli/src/daemon.rs: `slinger daemon info` (text and --json per docs/cli.md) and `slinger daemon stop` (says nothing on success). Add both to the table in docs/cli.md; run the tests in crates/cli/src/tests/guide.rs and update the guide's command list if it is generated from the commands.
- docs/service.md: both verbs in the verb table with a short "The daemon's own verbs" section; under "Versioning" say that `v` stays 1 and that a daemon older than these verbs answers `bad_request`, which a client reads as "older build". docs/app-parity.md: one row for the two commands naming the later app step (the restart offer). ARCHITECTURE.md: "Inside the daemon" and one row in the Boundaries table. CHANGELOG.
Tests: control wire tests; a new crates/daemon/src/tests/daemon.rs through a real socket: every info field (pid is this process, socket and data_dir are the ones served, claude follows the search of the earlier step); a request made before the stop still gets its reply; after `daemon_stop` serve returns and the socket file is gone. crates/daemon/tests/signals.rs with the real binary: `daemon_stop` exits 0 and takes the socket name back. CLI tests in crates/cli/src/tests for both commands, text and --json.

steps.title: bundle: slingerd and slinger inside slinger.app; --install symlinks the CLI into ~/.local/bin
steps.description:
Why: scripts/bundle.sh puts only slinger-app in the bundle (lines 29-35) and --install copies slingerd and slinger to ~/.local/bin as separate files (42-52): two install locations that drift. Owner decision: one location, the binaries inside the .app, the CLI symlinked.
Change scripts/bundle.sh:
- Always build the three release binaries. Copy slingerd and slinger to Contents/MacOS beside slinger-app. This path is a contract the app step relies on: `<bundle>/Contents/MacOS/slingerd`.
- Sign the two helpers ad hoc first, then the bundle, then `codesign --verify --strict` the bundle; fail loudly (✗ line, non-zero exit) if a binary is missing or the check fails.
- crates/app/Info.plist: CFBundleVersion becomes `@BUILD@`, filled with the commit count (`git rev-list --count HEAD`, an integer that grows; the package version when there is no git). CFBundleShortVersionString stays `@VERSION@`. Pass SLINGER_BUILD_SHA through untouched so all three binaries carry one stamp.
- --install: copy the app to SLINGER_APP_DIR (default /Applications) as today (remove, then copy); then for slinger and slingerd remove whatever is at SLINGER_BIN_DIR/<name> (a file from an older install, or a link) and make a symlink to the binary inside the installed app. It stops and restarts nothing: the app offers that (a later step). Print the app's path as today.
- Rewrite the header comment (lines 2-12): it says the app neither ships nor starts slingerd.
Check, do not assume: slingerd run through the symlink still finds the CLI beside it (`beside_me`, crates/daemon/src/lib.rs:158-161, uses current_exe); if macOS resolves it differently fix `beside_me` with a unit test over a pure function. .github/workflows/release.yml runs scripts/bundle.sh (line 94): keep that job valid.
Tests (bundle.sh is not part of check-all): a unit test in crates/app (a small new test file; crates/app/src/tests.rs is 459 lines) that Info.plist holds `@VERSION@`, `@BUILD@` and CFBundleExecutable slinger-app; the script's own verification above. You may run `scripts/bundle.sh` (no --install) to check the layout; never --install, and never open the bundle.
Docs in the same commit: README.md lines 32-37 (what --install does now), docs/service.md "Running it as a system service" first sentences, AGENTS.md Layout (the line on scripts/bundle.sh), CHANGELOG.

steps.title: app: start the bundled slingerd when none answers; show 'Starting slingerd…', not a shell hint
steps.description:
Why: with no daemon the window is dead and shows `✗ slingerd does not answer on <socket>` with the hint `start it with 'slingerd --socket …'` (crates/control/src/client.rs:306-310) in the focused pane (scene.rs:211-216), the message again in the sidebar (scene/sidebar.rs:169-172, 281-284), and once per canvas follower (backend/follow.rs:85-89). Owner decisions: the app starts the bundled slingerd when none answers; slingerd outlives the app.
Pure decisions (new crates/app/src/launch.rs, unit tests with a passed-in clock, no IO):
- `bundled(exe: &Path) -> Option<PathBuf>`: `<X>.app/Contents/MacOS/slingerd` when exe is `<X>.app/Contents/MacOS/slinger-app`; None for a bare binary (target/debug/slinger-app, cargo run, tests). A bare binary never starts a daemon.
- Managed only when: there is a bundled slingerd that is a file, the config sets no `[daemon] socket`, the default data directory is known, and the app is not in --preview. Not managed: exactly today's behaviour.
- A state machine: Up; Down -> spawn -> Starting{since}; Starting -> Up when the socket answers; the child exiting 4 (another slingerd holds the lock: the race) is not a failure, keep waiting; any other exit, or 10 s with no answer -> Failed{why}; Failed tries again after 30 s; Up -> Down when the socket stops answering (a daemon that died is started again). One child at a time. "Down" means a connect to the app's socket (Settings::socket) is refused or the file is missing; a daemon that accepts but answers slowly is running (slinger-2f9883) and is never Down.
- What to show per state: Starting = one line "Starting slingerd…" in the muted colour, no ✗, no hint; Failed = "✗ slingerd did not start" with the exit code if any, hint "see <log path>".
IO (new crates/app/src/backend/daemon.rs; first move `Watch` out of crates/app/src/backend.rs, 497 lines, into backend/watch.rs as a pure move): a thread that checks the socket about once a second, runs the state machine, and on spawn runs `<bundle>/Contents/MacOS/slingerd --log <default data dir>/slingerd.log` with no --socket and no --data-dir (the defaults; never --scratch), stdin, stdout and stderr null, in its own process group (std CommandExt::process_group(0)) so it outlives the app; a thread waits on the child to reap it and report its exit code. The spawn is behind a small trait or closure so tests replace it. The app sends nothing to the daemon when it quits.
Window: while Starting or Failed, the launch line replaces the daemon-unreachable problems in the focused pane (shared.trouble and the followers' problems; a config problem still shows) and the sidebar's ✗ line; the Save flash says "Not saved yet: slingerd is starting". Decide in scene (a new scene/daemon.rs or in scene/sidebar), draw with the existing labels: no new platform code. main.rs (473), window.rs (495), scene.rs (496) and scene/sidebar.rs (470) are at the 500-line cap: put new code in new modules and move code out by concept where needed.
Tests: launch.rs table tests for every transition above and for `bundled`; scene tests: Starting shows the one muted line and no ✗ in pane and sidebar, Failed shows ✗ and the log hint, not managed shows today's text; backend/daemon.rs tests: a stub program proves the argv and that exit 4 and exit 1 are reported apart; with a spawner that serves the daemon library in-process (the app dev-depends on slingerd) on a tempdir socket and data directory, the state reaches Up and the Watch gets workspaces. No test starts a real slingerd binary on the default data directory.
Docs in the same commit: docs/service.md "Socket" (the bullet "The app finds the daemon the same way": add that the bundled app starts one); ARCHITECTURE.md "Inside the app" and a Boundaries row (a bare slinger-app never starts a daemon: held by the launch.rs tests); AGENTS.md conventions: opening a bundle starts a daemon on the default data directory when none runs, so to hand-check a bundle against a scratch daemon give it a config (SLINGER_CONFIG) whose `[daemon] socket` names that daemon; CHANGELOG.
Hand checks (lines in docs/hand-check.md, under a heading "## Launcher (plan <this plan id>)"): (1) with no slingerd running, open /Applications/slinger.app: "Starting slingerd…" then the canvases, no terminal used; quit the app: slingerd and a working agent keep running; reopen: the window finds it. (2) kill -9 the daemon with the app open: it is back within seconds and unsent ink is sent. (3) open two copies of the app at once with no daemon: one slingerd runs. (4) a workspace under ~/Documents opened through the app-started daemon: which macOS prompt appears and for whom; does the grant survive a reinstall (the bundle is signed ad hoc).

steps.title: app: notice a slingerd of another build and offer to restart it; 'Restart slingerd' command
steps.description:
Why: after an update the old daemon keeps running (scripts/bundle.sh header: "keeps the old build until it is restarted") and nothing says so. Stopping slingerd ends its agents' processes (docs/service.md "Clean stop"), so the app asks; it never restarts by itself.
Pure (crates/app/src/launch.rs or a sibling, unit tests): `skew(mine, theirs) -> Same | Differs { daemon: String } | Old`: Same when `version` and `build` of `daemon_info` equal the app's own `control::build::PACKAGE` and `control::build::stamp()`; Old when the daemon answers `bad_request` to `daemon_info` (it predates the verb); an unreachable daemon is no answer, ask again later. The offer exists only when the app is managed (it has a bundled slingerd to start, and no `[daemon] socket`).
Backend (crates/app/src/backend/daemon.rs): ask `daemon_info` each time the state turns Up and each time the socket changes; publish the skew with the daemon's pid.
Window: a notice that stays until dismissed (the bar in crates/app/src/scene/sidebar/notice.rs): "slingerd is another build (<daemon build>; this app is <app build>)" with the action "Restart slingerd", and when agents' processes run, "ends N running agents" (the sidebar knows them). Dismissed: not shown again for that daemon pid.
Command `restart-daemon`, "Restart slingerd", in `Command::ALL` (crates/app/src/commands/registry.rs: palette, key overlay, the slinger menu in commands/menu.rs; no default key; add it to config.example.toml if the test that keeps that file in step with the parser asks). Managed: send `daemon_stop`; the launch loop of the earlier step sees the socket go and starts the bundled slingerd, and the window shows "Starting slingerd…". Not managed: flash why not ("slinger did not start this slingerd: restart it where it runs"). Old: flash that this slingerd cannot be stopped from here and must be stopped with SIGTERM once.
Files at the cap: window.rs (495), scene.rs (496); new code in new modules. Update the row in docs/app-parity.md added with the verbs.
Tests: the skew table; scene tests for the notice (text, agent count, dismiss, not managed shows none); command tests in crates/app/src/commands/tests.rs; a backend test with the daemon library in-process and the test spawner: `restart-daemon` ends the first daemon and a second answers with another `started_ms`; a daemon without the verb reads as Old.
Docs in the same commit: ARCHITECTURE.md "Inside the app"; CHANGELOG.
Hand check (one line in docs/hand-check.md, under a heading "## Launcher (plan <this plan id>)"): install a newer build with `scripts/bundle.sh --install` while slingerd runs, quit and reopen the app: the notice names both builds and the running agents; Restart slingerd brings the window back on the new daemon (`slinger daemon info` shows the new build and the exe inside the app); canvases and waiting slings are intact.

steps.title: bundle: an app icon (slinger.icns, CFBundleIconFile)
steps.description:

name: Launcher: the app starts slingerd; one install

sections.context: A workspace switch takes about 0.5 to 2 s and shows the wrong thing while it waits (seed slinger-eaa98b, audit of 2026-11-20). The cause is polling, not IO, and it was verified in the code: a sidebar tap only sets a mutex (app backend.rs:136-138); the Watch thread reads it after a 1 s sleep (backend.rs:69,129); the main thread takes news from every backend thread only on its 0.5 s tick (platform/mod.rs:73, route.rs:79, main.rs:177-182), once for the layout and once more for the page. The timings are read from code and were never measured. Second, a pane has no identity: the app numbers panes by their place in a tree it rebuilds for every layout (panes.rs:53-62, layout/tree.rs:68-72) and keys each pane's view by that number alone (canvases.rs:72,429). So a switch gives the new canvas the old pane's pan and zoom and draws the old canvas's last scene until the new page comes (canvases.rs:448-457); closing a pane shifts the other panes' views; focus carries over by number (shared.rs:91). Third, nothing about where a pane looks is kept: every launch is page 1 at 100% at the origin (layout.rs:104-107), a split starts the new pane there too (canvases.rs:440-444), and there is no way back to the content but panning. Owner decisions (2026-11-20, not reopened): view state (page, pan, zoom, focus per pane) lives in the daemon; reopening restores the last view; a first open fits the content; pane splits stay with the workspace.
sections.approach:
Measure first, then remove the waits, then give panes identity, then keep views.

1. A trace line (SLINGER_TRACE=switch) goes in first, so the owner has a baseline and each later step shows its gain.
2. Waits: one small pure module, backend/wake.rs, gives every backend thread a channel whose send wakes the main thread; platform supplies only the function that posts Event::Wake to the main run loop. The 0.5 s timer stays as a clock (config stat, fades, the pill's seconds) and as the backstop for a wake that arrives while the answer is busy; it is no longer the path for news. The Watch waits on a condvar that want() notifies, and tells the layout before it asks for the agents list. It keeps a 1 s round for pane changes made outside the app, because the daemon has no layout feed.
3. Identity: the core layout gives each pane a stable id, stored in the layout text (version 2: "canvas:main@3" and a next id) and sent in the pane tree. Pane verbs still name panes by number. The app uses the id as its PaneId and keeps views and focus per workspace, so nothing leaks between workspaces or shifts on a close, and a pane never draws another canvas's last scene.
4. Views: a pure Viewport::fitting places a view the first time its page comes, and backs a zoom-to-fit command. A split copies the source view. The core module workspace/view.rs owns the stored view (canvas, page, origin, zoom) and focus per pane id; the daemon keeps them in workspaces/views.json in its data directory, returns them in every pane reply, copies them on pane_open and prunes them on close; one new verb, pane_view, sets them. The app applies a stored view only to a pane it holds no view for, and sends its views through a worker 300 ms after the last change, on a switch and at quit.

Why this shape: each decision has one home (wake in wake.rs, pane identity in core panes.rs, the stored view in core view.rs, placement in layout.rs), platform gains two translations and no decision, and each step leaves main working with check-all green. Views ride in the pane reply instead of a second verb so the layout and its views arrive together and the first paint is already at the restored place.

Not in this plan: incremental scene building and pen latency, a canvas listing UI, a cache of followed canvases for other workspaces (after the waits are gone a switch costs one canvas_show; the trace will say if more is needed), moving the split ratios out of the workspace file, keyboard workspace switching, and timing inside the daemon. The box trail is kept in memory per workspace but is not stored.

alternatives.name: Key the app's views by (workspace, position) or by (canvas, page) and leave the core alone
alternatives.rejected_because: Position still shifts when a pane closes or an agent opens one, and a (canvas, page) key makes two panes on one page share a view. The owner chose per-pane views kept by the daemon, which needs an id the daemon and the app agree on.

alternatives.name: Keep pane ids in the daemon's data directory, beside the views, and leave the layout text at version 1
alternatives.rejected_because: Ids would be tied to positions in a file that other programs and other machines change, so they would have to be re-matched after every outside edit. An id in the text is the only one that survives. The cost is a layout version an older slingerd does not read (it shows one pane); see the risks.

alternatives.name: Remove the 0.5 s timer entirely
alternatives.rejected_because: The flash, the sidebar notice and the sling pill change with time, the config files are found by stat, and platform drops an event that arrives while the answer runs, so a wake can be lost. The timer stays as the clock and the backstop; news no longer waits for it.

alternatives.name: Send the layout before the agent UI code, as the audit proposed
alternatives.rejected_because: Watch::uis documents that a layout's UIs come before the layout, and a UI pane has nothing to show without its code. Only the agents list, which nothing in the layout needs, moves after the layout.

alternatives.name: A separate verb to read views (view_list) and keep the pane reply as it is
alternatives.rejected_because: Two round trips, and the layout could be drawn before its views arrive, which shows the fitted view and then jumps. One reply with optional fields is one path; the Watch compares the arrangement only, so saves do not echo.

alternatives.name: Keep views in the app's user defaults
alternatives.rejected_because: Decided by the owner: the daemon keeps them, so agents and the CLI can see where the user looks and a reinstall loses nothing.

alternatives.name: Keep following every open workspace's canvases so a switch needs no round trip
alternatives.rejected_because: More threads and daemon connections for a gain the trace has not shown to be needed. Revisit with numbers after the wake.

steps.title: app: a timing trace line for a workspace switch (SLINGER_TRACE=switch)
steps.description:
Goal: one stderr line per workspace switch that shows where the time goes, so the audit's timings (read from code, never measured) are confirmed before and after the next steps. It goes first on purpose: it gives the baseline.

Behaviour: with the environment variable SLINGER_TRACE containing "switch" (read once in crates/app/src/main.rs; unset means no cost and no output), a pick of another workspace (sidebar tap, open-workspace, the config's workspace changing: every place that calls Watch::want) starts a trace. It prints one line when the first scene is drawn in which every canvas pane of the new layout has its page, for example: "switch notes: watch +612ms, layout +640ms, taken +1000ms, shown +1004ms, heard +1500ms, drawn +1512ms". Phases, each a time since the pick: watch (the Watch thread read the wanted name), layout (the Watch sent the layout), taken (the main thread took the layout), shown (a Follower got its canvas_show reply; the last one of the new panes), heard (the main thread took that News::Shown in Canvases::poll), drawn (the scene was handed to the platform). A new pick before the line is printed replaces the trace. A layout with no canvas pane prints at "taken".

Where: a new pure module crates/app/src/trace.rs owns the phases and the line's text (no IO; main.rs writes the line to stderr, as it does the pen's delay log at main.rs:460-466). The Watch thread (crates/app/src/backend.rs:105-133) stamps "watch" and "layout" with Instant and sends them with the layout; the Follower (crates/app/src/backend/follow.rs:91-94) stamps the time of its Shown. backend.rs is 497 lines and the cap is 500: first move Watch, load and tell, with their tests, to crates/app/src/backend/watch.rs (a pure move, re-exported from backend), then add the stamps. main.rs is 473 lines: keep the wiring short or move the news-taking part of the step closure to its own function.

Tests: trace.rs unit tests with fixed Instants (the line's text; a second pick replaces the first; nothing without the flag; a layout with no canvas pane). A test with the real daemon helper (backend::tests::with_daemon, crates/app/src/backend/testing.rs) that a Watch's layout carries its two stamps in order and a Follower's Shown carries one.

Docs: ARCHITECTURE.md "Inside the app" (new trace.rs row; backend/watch.rs). CHANGELOG is not needed (no user-visible change).

Hand check (add to docs/hand-check.md, new heading "## Switching and views (slinger-eaa98b)"): "open target/slinger.app --env SLINGER_TRACE=switch --stderr <file>, tap between two workspaces ten times, paste the lines in the seed: the baseline before the wake". Not in scope: timing inside the daemon (the audit's converse log).

steps.title: app: backend threads wake the main thread, so news does not wait for the 0.5 s tick
steps.description:
Problem (verified): news from every backend thread reaches the window only on Event::Tick, every POLL_SECONDS = 0.5 (crates/app/src/platform/mod.rs:73,237,378; crates/app/src/route.rs:79; main.rs:177-182). A switch pays two ticks (layout, then News::Shown), a PDF backdrop a third (canvases/pdf.rs:92).

Add:
1. crates/app/src/backend/wake.rs, pure. Wake is Clone + Send + Sync. Wake::new(post) wraps a function that asks the main thread to look; Wake::none() does nothing (tests, preview). wake() calls post unless a wake is already pending; taken() clears the pending mark. wake.channel::<T>() returns (Teller<T>, Receiver<T>); Teller::send sends and then wakes, so no thread can send news and forget to wake.
2. Every backend thread makes its news channel with wake.channel(): Watch (three channels), Follower (backend/follow.rs), Outbox (backend/outbox.rs), Slinger (backend/sling.rs), feedback (backend/feedback.rs), Flick (backend/flick.rs), Lives (canvases/live.rs), Pdfs and the open-pdf thread (canvases/pdf.rs). Pass the Wake through Watch::start and Canvases::new (or a builder beside Canvases::rendering); Canvases::reconnect keeps it.
3. platform: a new Event::Wake and a safe function platform::waker() that returns the post function. It may be called from any thread and makes the main run loop dispatch Event::Wake, in the common run-loop modes so it arrives during a pen stroke or a divider drag as the timer does (chrome.rs:60-72). Use what the crate already links (block2, objc2-foundation); platform only translates. platform/mod.rs is 498 lines: move Event and Step to crates/app/src/platform/event.rs (re-exported) in this step.
4. route.rs: Event::Wake takes the same path as Event::Tick (Routed::News(false)). In main.rs the news path calls wake.taken() before it drains the channels, so a send that races the drain posts again. The preview window's answer (main.rs:126) treats Wake as Tick.

The tick stays, as a clock only: it stats the config files, fades the flash and the sidebar notice, ticks the sling pill, retries a missed PDF, and it is the backstop for a wake that came while the answer was running (dispatch drops such an event: platform/mod.rs:303-304; this is why the pending mark is cleared on the main thread and not by the sender). Say so in the comment on POLL_SECONDS.

Keep the trace line of step 1 working: "taken" and "heard" now follow "layout" and "shown" by milliseconds.

Tests: wake.rs units (two wakes post once; after taken() the next wake posts; Teller::send wakes after the value is in the channel; none() is silent). follow.rs with the real daemon: a Follower given a counting Wake posts for Shown and for a change. route test: Event::Wake returns Routed::News. Every existing test passes Wake::none().

Docs: ARCHITECTURE.md (main.rs and backend.rs rows near lines 382-442, the threading and config paragraphs near 1198-1208, platform row, layer table if a boundary moves); the module comments of backend/follow.rs and platform/mod.rs; CHANGELOG under Unreleased, Changed: what an agent draws and a workspace switch show at once.

Hand check (add to docs/hand-check.md, new heading "## Switching and views (slinger-eaa98b)"): "in the bundle: an agent's 'slinger canvas put' appears with no half-second step, also while a pen stroke or a divider drag is under way; the trace line shows taken and heard a few ms after layout and shown; the app idles at no more CPU than before".

steps.title: app: the Watch wakes when a workspace is picked; the agents list no longer delays the layout
steps.description:
Problem (verified): Watch::want only sets a mutex (crates/app/src/backend.rs:136-138, in backend/watch.rs after step 1). The thread reads it after its sleep of EVERY = 1 s (backend.rs:69,129), and in each round it asks session_list and workspace_list (workspaces(), backend/agents.rs) before it tells the layout (backend.rs:123-125).

Change:
1. The thread waits on a Condvar paired with the wanted workspace, with EVERY as the timeout. want() and Watch::follow(socket) set their value and notify, so the next round starts at once. The 1 s round stays for changes made outside the app (an agent's 'slinger pane open'): the daemon has no feed of layouts.
2. Order of a round: pane layout; when it changed, the code of its agent UIs; tell the UIs, then the layout; then workspaces() and tell the agents. Keep the UI code ahead of its layout: Watch::uis documents "A layout's UIs come before the layout" (backend.rs:145-146) and a UI pane has nothing to show without it. Only the agents list moves after the layout.
3. Make the round a function that takes the daemon and a sink, so a test can record the order of what is told.

Keep the thread's end rule (it ends once nobody listens) and the trace's "watch" and "layout" stamps.

Tests (real daemon helper, two open workspaces): with the round time set long for the test (for example 30 s through a test-only constructor), want(B) brings B's layout within a few seconds: this proves the notify and not the timeout. The round tells UIs, layout, agents in that order. A pane opened from elsewhere is still heard within EVERY (the existing test a_watch_hears_a_pane_opened_elsewhere_in_the_workspace_it_wants). Dropping the Watch ends the thread.

Docs: ARCHITECTURE.md backend.rs row ("every second on a thread of its own") and the paragraph near line 1206; CHANGELOG, Changed: a tap on a workspace shows it at once.

Hand check (add to docs/hand-check.md, new heading "## Switching and views (slinger-eaa98b)"): "in the bundle with SLINGER_TRACE=switch: tap between two workspaces; 'drawn' is under about 50 ms warm; paste ten lines in the seed beside the baseline".

steps.title: core, control, daemon, CLI: stable pane ids in the workspace layout (layout version 2)
steps.description:
Problem (verified): a pane has no identity. The layout text is "row 0.5 canvas:a ui:b" (crates/core/src/workspace/panes.rs:1-11) and a pane is named by a number that moves when panes open and close (docs/service.md "Panes"). The app can only key its per-pane state by position, which is the root of the view leaks.

Core (crates/core/src/workspace/panes.rs, 381 lines; move the text reading and writing to workspace/panes/text.rs if the file would pass 500):
- Each pane has an id: a u32 of 1 or more, unique in its layout, never given again in that layout. Layout keeps the next id. Layout::new gives id 1. Layout::open gives the new pane the next id. close and resize leave every other id as it was.
- Layout text version 2 (panes::VERSION = 2): a pane's word is "canvas:main@3"; the [layout] table holds version = 2, panes = "<text>" and next = <n>.
- Reading never fails for an id reason: version 1 text (no ids) gets 1..n in order; in version 2 a word with no id, a 0, or an id already used gets a fresh id; a missing or too-small next becomes the highest id + 1.
- Workspace::panes (crates/core/src/workspace.rs:271-280) reads versions 1 and 2; set_panes (285-290) writes version 2 and next, and keeps the table's other fields as it does today. A version 1 file is rewritten only by the first change to its panes; until then its ids are 1..n by position, which is what that write stores.
- Pane::word() for the record's pane_moved stays "canvas:notes", with no id: the record's contract does not change.

Control (crates/control/src/pane.rs): Pane gets "id" (#[serde(default)], so a reply from an older daemon reads as 0). The pane verbs still name a pane by its number.

Daemon (crates/daemon/src/server/pane.rs wire()): fill the id. CLI: 'slinger pane list --json' carries the id through serde; the text lines stay number, kind, target.

Tests: core panes tests (close the first of "row A B": B keeps its id; an id is not reused after close, also across encode and decode; version 1 text reads as 1..n and writes as version 2; missing, zero and duplicate ids are repaired; next is repaired; round trip). core workspace tests (a version 1 file read, changed and written as version 2 with next; other [layout] fields kept; a version 3 layout still falls back to one pane). control wire-line tests with and without id. daemon tests/pane.rs through the socket (ids stay across open, close and resize, and across a daemon restart on the same data directory). CLI test: the JSON has id.

Docs, same commit: docs/workspace.md "[layout]" (version 2, the id, next, what an older slingerd does with it: it shows one pane and replaces the layout at its next pane change, the rule already at docs/workspace.md:84-86); docs/service.md "Panes" (the id in the tree, numbers still name panes); ARCHITECTURE.md; docs/cli.md pane list JSON; CHANGELOG, Changed. crates/cli/src/guide.md only if it shows pane JSON.

steps.title: app: key panes by the server's ids; views and focus per workspace; no old canvas in a new pane
steps.description:
Problem (verified): Panes::follow builds a fresh Tree whose first pane is always PaneId(0) (crates/app/src/panes.rs:53-62, layout/tree.rs:68-72). Canvases keeps views by PaneId alone (canvases.rs:72,429). So after a workspace switch the new canvas gets the old pane's pan and zoom and the pane draws view.last, the old canvas's scene, until the new page comes (canvases.rs:448-457); closing the first of two panes gives the second the first's view; Shared::follow keeps the focus number across workspaces (shared.rs:91).

Change:
1. Panes::follow gives each pane the PaneId of its server id (control Pane.id from the step before). Tree needs a way to split with a given id; its own counter starts above the highest id, for the window's own splits when there is no workspace. A layout whose ids are 0 (an older daemon) falls back to today's build-order ids. crates/app/src/layout/ has a 100% line-coverage floor (budgets/coverage-budgets.json): test every new line.
2. Move View and its bookkeeping out of canvases.rs (497 lines) into crates/app/src/canvases/view.rs. A View knows the canvas it is for. When its pane shows another canvas, the view starts again (start viewport, first page, nothing drawn, no reader column, no trail).
3. Views are per workspace. Canvases learns the workspace the panes are for (an argument of Canvases::show or a field of Panes; take the smaller change) and, when it changes, parks the views under the old name and brings back those parked under the new one. Parked views are pruned to the layout's ids the next time their workspace is shown. No workspace (no daemon) is one more key.
4. A pane whose page has not come draws nothing of another canvas: an empty paper scene, or no scene, never view.last of a different canvas or workspace. The rule "a pane turned to a page still on its way keeps what it drew" stays for a page turn inside one canvas. Check the platform side by reading only: it keeps one CanvasView per PaneId and removes it when no scene names the pane (platform/mod.rs:414-434), so equal ids in two workspaces must not show the old picture.
5. Focus is per workspace and by id. Shared::follow: for the same workspace, focus stays on the same id, or, when that pane is gone, goes to the pane now at its old number (today's rule); for another workspace, to the pane that had focus there earlier in this run, else the first.
6. Go through the other state keyed by PaneId and make a switch safe for each: Canvases.pen, handle, steps and turning; Shared.menu (close it); the web views' key (platform/web.rs:178-182, by pane and item).
7. canvases/kept.rs:48,64 keeps PaneId::number on disk for a pane waiting for a page (slinger-857848). It now holds the server's id, which is stable. Update the comments at layout/tree.rs:33-38 and ARCHITECTURE.md near line 1249. A file written by an older build may name a pane by position: the worst case is a pane that does not turn.

Tests (pure: canvases/tests.rs or canvases/view tests, shared/tests.rs, panes tests, layout/tree/tests.rs): close A in "row A B": B keeps its viewport, page and trail. Workspace A, then B, then A, with equal pane ids in both: B's pane starts with a new view; back in A the viewport, page and trail are as left. Before B's page comes, show() returns no draw that came from A. A pane opened by someone else (a new layout through follow) moves no other view. Focus per workspace. The id-0 fallback.

Docs: ARCHITECTURE.md app rows (panes.rs, canvases, layout/tree). CHANGELOG, Fixed: a workspace no longer opens at another workspace's zoom and scroll or shows its ink; closing a pane no longer moves the other panes' views.

Hand check (add to docs/hand-check.md, new heading "## Switching and views (slinger-eaa98b)"): "in the bundle: zoom in on workspace A, tap B: B is not zoomed and never shows A's ink; tap A: it is where you left it; split, pan the right pane, close the left: the right one keeps its place".

steps.title: app: a first open fits the content; a zoom-to-fit command
steps.description:
Owner decision: a first open fits the content. Today every view starts at Viewport::start(): origin 16 points in, 100% (crates/app/src/layout.rs:104-107), whatever the page holds, and the zoom commands are in, out and 100% only (canvases/paging.rs:47-54).

steps.title: core, control, daemon: the daemon keeps per-pane views and focus; a pane_view verb
steps.description:
Owner decisions: view state (page, pan, zoom, and the focused pane) lives in the daemon; pane splits stay with the workspace file. Follow "Adding a verb" in docs/service.md: core, then crates/control, then the daemon's answer, then clients.

Core, new crates/core/src/workspace/view.rs (owns the format and the rules; no IO):
- PaneView { canvas, page: Option<String>, x, y, zoom }: the canvas and page the pane looked at, the canvas point at the pane's top left, and the zoom.
- Views { focus: Option<pane id>, panes: map from pane id to PaneView } for one workspace.
- Rules: set(id, view) refuses a number that is not finite or a zoom of 0 or less (Error::Invalid with a hint); keep(ids) drops the views of panes not in the layout and a focus that names none; copy(from, to); view_of(id, target) gives a view only when its canvas is what the pane shows now. Text form: JSON with a version; text that cannot be read is no views, never an error.

Daemon, new crates/daemon/src/views.rs (workspaces.rs is 493 lines): one file, workspaces/views.json in the data directory, {"v":1,"workspaces":{"<directory of the workspace's file>":<Views>}}, keyed by the directory because that is how the daemon knows an open workspace (workspaces/open.json). Written whole and synced when it changes, one change at a time. Never in slinger-workspace.toml and never in a canvas file. A missing or unreadable file is no views. A view change appends no event to the record: the log is append-only and views change often. Closing a workspace keeps its views, so opening it again restores them.

Control (crates/control/src/pane.rs, 241 lines): PaneAsk::PaneView { workspace, views: [{id, canvas, page?, x, y, zoom}], focus? }, written by the same small type as the other pane verbs (the app builds no Request: docs/service.md step 2). Pane gets an optional "view"; PaneLayout gets an optional "focus" (a pane id). Client::pane_view. All additions are optional fields, so the protocol version stays 1.

Daemon answer (crates/daemon/src/server/pane.rs): every pane reply carries each pane's stored view (when its canvas is the pane's target) and the focus. pane_view stores the views and focus it names and replies as pane_list does; an id that is not in the layout is ignored and the verb still succeeds. pane_open beside a pane copies that pane's stored view to the new id when both show the same target. pane_close and any change prune views to the layout's ids.

Clients: the app sends pane_view in the next step. The CLI gets no new command (an agent has no use for setting the user's view); 'slinger pane list --json' shows view and focus through serde, which lets an agent see where the user looks.

Tests: core view tests (each rule; round trip; unreadable text). control wire-line tests for the new ask and for replies with and without view and focus. daemon tests/pane.rs through a real socket: set then list returns the view and focus; they survive a daemon restart on the same data directory; pane_close prunes; pane_open beside copies; an unknown id is ignored; a zoom of 0 is "invalid"; two workspaces do not share views; pane_view leaves the bytes of slinger-workspace.toml unchanged and appends no event.

Docs, same commit: docs/service.md (the verb table, "Panes", and "Data directory": workspaces/views.json); ARCHITECTURE.md (core workspace/view.rs, daemon views.rs, server/pane.rs row near line 283, control); SPEC.md section 5 line 63 ("It holds no durable state"): the server keeps the arrangement and the views, the app keeps only its window chrome (frame, sidebar, last workspace) in the user defaults; docs/cli.md pane list JSON; CHANGELOG.

steps.title: app: restore each pane's view and the focus from the daemon; save them as they change
steps.description:
Owner decision: reopening restores the last view. This step makes the app read the views the daemon keeps (the step before) and send its own.

Read:
- The Watch's layout news carries the stored views and focus (they are in the pane_list reply). The Watch decides "the layout changed" on the arrangement only (workspace, tree, ids, targets, ratios) and ignores view and focus, so the app's own saves do not come back as layout news and do not fetch the UI code again (backend.rs:118-121 fetches it for every fresh layout).
- When a pane of (workspace, id) has no view in memory (first sight in this run, or a pane someone else opened), it takes the stored view if that view's canvas is the pane's: page, origin and zoom, the zoom held in MIN_ZOOM..=MAX_ZOOM by a Viewport constructor in layout.rs (100% coverage floor). Such a view is placed: the first-open fit does not run. With no stored view the pane is unplaced and fits its content. A view in memory always wins over a stored one.
- The first time a workspace is shown in this run, focus goes to the stored focus, if that pane is there.
- A PDF pane needs nothing more: the reader refits its column on each draw and keeps the top (Viewport::reading), so the stored origin restores the scroll.
- The box trail is not stored: a relaunch opens outside the box.

Write:
- A pure function gives the current workspace's looks: for each canvas pane its id, canvas, the page it shows (the page's id once it has come) and viewport, and the focused pane's id. main.rs compares it with the last one handed over after an event that drew, and hands a changed one to a new worker, crates/app/src/backend/views.rs (shaped like Outbox: the main thread never waits). The worker waits until 300 ms pass with no newer looks, then sends one pane_view with the panes that changed. A failed send is tried again with the next looks and is otherwise dropped: a lost view is not worth a problem on screen. Build the worker over a send function so a unit test can count requests.
- A switch to another workspace sends the old workspace's looks without the wait.
- Quit: the red close button ends the app without the answer hearing of it (crates/app/src/platform/mod.rs:275-280), and Step::Quit goes the same way (mod.rs:320). Add Event::Quitting, dispatched in close_and_quit before terminate (platform only translates; if the window-lifecycle work has added a quit event by then, use that one). The answer hands over the looks and waits for the worker at most 500 ms: the client's own timeout is 30 s (crates/control/src/client.rs:25), so wait on the thread, not on the call.

Mind the caps: main.rs 473 lines, canvases.rs after step 5, platform/mod.rs after step 2.

Tests: with the real daemon helper: pan, zoom and turn the page, flush, and pane_list has the view; a new Canvases that follows that layout shows the pane on the stored page at the stored viewport, with no fit; a stored view for another canvas is ignored; a view in memory wins over a later layout's stored view; a pane_view sent from elsewhere gives no layout news from the Watch; focus is restored. Worker unit tests: many looks inside the wait make one request with only the changed panes; the flush at quit sends at once and returns within its bound when the daemon does not answer.

Docs: ARCHITECTURE.md (backend/views.rs, the Watch's news, Event::Quitting, canvases/view.rs); CHANGELOG, Added: a pane opens on the page, pan and zoom you left it at, on this machine, after a switch, a relaunch or a daemon restart.

Hand check (add to docs/hand-check.md, new heading "## Switching and views (slinger-eaa98b)"): "in the bundle: in two workspaces set a page, a zoom and a focused pane; quit with cmd+Q, open: all as left; again with the red button; restart slingerd: all as left; a PDF pane returns to its scroll place; a pane an agent opens beside yours starts at your place".

risks: The audit's timings were never measured. If the trace of step 1 shows the time is elsewhere (canvas_show on a large canvas, the scene build), steps 2 and 3 gain less than expected; decide on the baseline before step 2 is merged.

Layout version 2 is not read by an older slingerd: on a machine that syncs slinger-workspace.toml and runs an older build, the workspace shows one pane and that build replaces the layout at its next pane change. Upgrade every machine that shares a workspace file together.

The wake must reach the run loop in the common modes, or news stalls during a pen stroke or a drag; and a wake that arrives while the answer is busy is dropped by platform, so the pending mark must be cleared on the main thread and the timer must stay. Only a hand check in the bundle proves the AppKit side.

Several files are at the 500-line cap: app backend.rs 497, canvases.rs 497, platform/mod.rs 498, window.rs 495, main.rs 473; daemon workspaces.rs 493. Each step names the split it needs; a step that skips the split fails check:size.
crates/app/src/layout.rs and layout/ have a 100% coverage floor, so every new line there (fitting, the stored-viewport constructor, the tree's id split) needs a test.
Other state keyed by PaneId (pen, handle, steps, turning, the page menu, web views, the unsent-ink file) may have a switch case the tests do not cover; step 5 lists them.
Save at quit depends on a new platform event from the window's close; the window-lifecycle track may add its own terminate hook. Use one event, whichever lands first.
views.json grows by one entry per workspace ever opened; entries are small and are not removed when a workspace closes, by design (reopen restores).

sd spawns each child seed from the step's title, type, priority, labels and blocks only. The "description" in each step of this file is accepted by the schema but is not copied to the child seed: copy each one to its seed after submit (sd update <id> --description) or point the workers at this file.
acceptance: With SLINGER_TRACE=switch the app prints one line per workspace switch with the time of each phase, and in the bundle a warm switch reaches "drawn" in about 50 ms or less (hand check).
No backend news waits for the 0.5 s timer: a test shows a Follower's news posts a wake, and Event::Wake runs the news path.
Watch::want brings the wanted workspace's layout without waiting for the 1 s round (test with the round time set long).
A pane keeps its id across open, close, resize and a daemon restart; a version 1 layout reads and is written as version 2; pane verbs still take numbers.

After a switch the new workspace's pane never draws the previous canvas and does not take its pan, zoom, page or focus; switching back shows the first workspace as it was left; closing a pane leaves the other panes' views in place (pure tests).
A pane with no stored view opens with its content in view at 100% or less; zoom-to-fit (cmd+9, palette, View menu) brings the content back.
A split shows the same page, pan, zoom and box as its source pane.

After a relaunch of the app and after a restart of slingerd, each pane of each workspace shows the page, pan and zoom it was left at, and focus is on the pane that had it; the workspace file is not written by a view change.
docs/service.md, docs/workspace.md, docs/cli.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, SPEC.md section 5 and CHANGELOG describe the new contracts; docs/hand-check.md has the lines each step names.
cargo xtask check-all is green after every step.

name: Switching and views: instant switch, stable pane ids, views that come back

sections.context:
The 2026-11-20 audit (seed slinger-6cb0db; reports context-menus, close-workspace, menus-keys, sidebar-nav, mac-native-feel) found that the app has no secondary click, that every command acts on implicit state (the focused pane, the selection, the workspace the window shows), that no menu item ever greys out, and that the menu bar lacks the standard Mac items.

Checked against the code at cc729fa: crates/app/src/platform/input.rs:111-124 turns a right or middle press into a pan only and never tells the app of a click; Pen (scene/ink.rs:71) carries no control bit; commands/menu.rs Item has no enabled field and platform/mod.rs validateMenuItem judges only cut, copy and paste; Sidebar::close (scene/sidebar.rs:240) closes only the shown workspace and takes the row out before the daemon answers (window.rs:136-137); a healthy sidebar row has no close control (sidebar.rs:330); the app menu is About, Reload config, Quit and nothing calls setWindowsMenu, setServicesMenu or setHelpMenu.

The owner's report that closing a workspace 'does not exist' is this: it exists (opt+cmd+W, File menu, palette) but not where workspaces are listed.

Owner decisions (do not reopen): the context menu is a native NSMenu opened on right-mouse-up below a movement threshold, so a right drag still pans; ctrl+click opens it too; close-workspace keeps its key (opt+cmd+W).

Out of scope: one command table (slinger-ffcb03), canvas rename and delete verbs, a recent list, the agent a close orphans (slinger-0f6923), the settings command (slinger-54ae6e), sidebar scrolling (slinger-d85d5a), the slow workspace switch (slinger-eaa98b), key changes, title case.
sections.approach:
One pure model, thin platform. Three pure pieces in crates/app/src/commands: (1) able.rs: Facts (what the window can act on now) and can(command, &Facts) -> bool, the one enabled predicate; (2) menu.rs: the menu bar, whose Item gains `enabled` from can, plus separators, more Native items and a role per menu; (3) context.rs: Subject (the thing under the pointer) and items(subject, keymap, checked, facts) -> Vec<Item>, the same Item the bar uses, titles from Command::title and keys from the live Keymap. platform/menu.rs only makes NSMenuItems from Items and pops the NSMenu a Step::Menu carries.

Subject: explicit, and justified per kind. A context menu is about one Subject, named in the type. For a pane, a footer, the empty canvas and canvas items, opening the menu focuses the pane and (Finder's rule) selects an unselected item under the pointer: those commands already take the focused pane and the selection as their subject, the user sees what the menu will act on, and a click there does the same. For a sidebar workspace row and a divider there is no cheap 'current': making a workspace current is the slow switch (and closing B must not first show B), and a divider has no focus. So for those the pick carries its Subject: the popup's items go to the app as Event::Picked(Command, Subject), and the workspace verbs (close, show folder, start, stop, restart agent) take a folder, the divider verbs a divider. The app keeps no 'last menu subject': a menu dismissed without a pick leaves nothing a later menu-bar command could act on by mistake. Workspaces are named by folder (unique, as workspace_close takes), never by row index.

Click against pan is decided in a pure module, not in platform. Platform sends the right and middle button's down, drag and up raw (Event::Button) and maps a ctrl+left press and its drags and lift onto the secondary button, as macOS defines ctrl+click. scene/secondary.rs holds the press and answers: a pan once the pointer has gone past a slop, a context click when a secondary press lifts inside it, never a click for the middle button. A click therefore no longer nudges the canvas. The app takes the right press everywhere but over an open entry field (which keeps its native text menu), so WebKit's own menu no longer shows over an agent UI.

Greyed items never change what a key does: AppKit does not fire a disabled item for its key, so the key reaches the keymap as any key does and the command answers as today (a flash that says why). can says no only where running the command now would do nothing or only refuse.

Close by target: the sidebar gets a close mark on every workspace row (always shown: the pen has no hover), close asks the daemon first and the row leaves only on success, and only closing the shown workspace changes what the window shows.

Order: the sidebar close first (the owner's complaint, no dependency), then the predicate and the standard menus (both menu-bar only), then the raw button events, then the popup with the subjects that need no explicit target, then items and the selection, then workspace rows and dividers with Event::Picked. Each step ends with cargo xtask check-all green, updates ARCHITECTURE.md and CHANGELOG.md in the same commit, and adds one line to docs/hand-check.md for what only a person can check.

House rules every step must hold: files stay under 500 lines, and window.rs (495), platform/mod.rs (498), canvases.rs (497), scene.rs (496), main.rs (473), scene/sidebar.rs (470), tests.rs (459), scene/sidebar/tests.rs (454) and commands.rs (454) are at the cap, so new code goes in new files split by concept (named in each step). Only crates/app/src/platform may hold unsafe, objc2 or AppKit and only main.rs may name crate::platform (budgets/layer-rules.json); route.rs gets Event and Step through main's re-export. The workspace coverage floor is 86%: platform code is not covered, so each step's logic sits in pure modules with tests. Tests go through route() with the World in crates/app/src/tests.rs and a real scratch daemon (backend::tests helpers), not through mocks. Each step's `description` field below is its full brief.

alternatives.name: Make the target current first, for every subject
alternatives.rejected_because: For a workspace row it means the slow workspace switch before a close, and 'Close' on row B would first show B. For a divider nothing is 'current'. It also keeps the split between what the sidebar and the panes think is shown (sidebar-nav finding 2) on the path of every row command.

alternatives.name: Remember the menu's subject in the app and apply it to the next Event::Command
alternatives.rejected_because: A menu dismissed without a pick leaves the subject behind, and the next menu-bar 'Close workspace' would close the wrong workspace. The pick carries its subject instead.

alternatives.name: Add a control bit to Pen and decide ctrl+click in the app
alternatives.rejected_because: Pen is built as a literal in 43 places, and ctrl+click being the secondary click is a macOS convention, so it is a translation. Platform maps it to the secondary button and one pure path serves both.

alternatives.name: Keep the pan in platform and send only Event::Context on mouse-up
alternatives.rejected_because: The slop is a decision, and a click would still pan the canvas by its jitter before the menu opens. The pure Secondary module withholds the pan until the slop is passed and is unit-tested.

alternatives.name: Reuse platform/menu.rs made() and Target::run: as they are for the popup (the audit's suggestion)
alternatives.rejected_because: run: sends Event::Command with no subject, and AppKit auto-enables any item whose target answers its action. The popup needs its enabled state from the pure model and, for rows and dividers, its subject.

alternatives.name: A drawn overlay menu like the page menu
alternatives.rejected_because: The owner chose a native NSMenu.

alternatives.name: A greyed 'Settings…' placeholder now
alternatives.rejected_because: slinger-54ae6e adds the real command on cmd+,; an item that never enables says something untrue. Step 3 leaves its place in the app menu (after About).

alternatives.name: Rebuild the menu bar whenever an enabled flag changes
alternatives.rejected_because: Facts change with every selection, and the timer fires while a menu is open. Platform keeps the NSMenu while the layout is the same and answers validateMenuItem: from the newest model.

steps.title: app: close a workspace from its sidebar row: a close mark per row, close by folder
steps.description:
Goal: every workspace row in the sidebar has a ✕ that closes that workspace without showing it first; close-workspace (opt+cmd+W, File menu, palette, a broken row's 'Close workspace' line) still closes the shown one. Key unchanged.

Files. crates/app/src/scene/sidebar.rs is 470 lines: first move the layout (`laid`, `Line`, `block`) into a new scene/sidebar/rows.rs, a pure move. scene/taps.rs: add `Tap::Close(usize)` (the sidebar's workspace with this index; resolved to its folder at the tap, as Tap::Workspace is). Sidebar: replace `close()` with `dir(index) -> Option<PathBuf>` (a lookup; `shown_dir` stays) and `closed(&mut self, dir: &Path) -> bool`, which takes that row out and returns whether it was the shown one (then `shown = None`, so `at()` picks as it does today). In the layout, each workspace's name line gets a ✕ in theme.muted at the sidebar's right edge with a target style::TAP (28 pt) wide and the row high; the name's label ends before it; these targets come before the row targets in the list, because Taps finds the first frame that holds the point, and the merge of a workspace's lines into one row target must still work. A collapsed sidebar has none. window.rs: `close_workspace` takes the folder, asks the daemon first (backend::close_workspace), on Ok calls `sidebar.closed` and flashes 'Closed <name>' (the folder's name for a nameless broken file), on Err flashes the problem and leaves the row; it returns whether the shown one closed. `tap()` gets a `Tap::Close(_) => {}` arm. route.rs: the arm for `Ask::Run(Command::CloseWorkspace)` passes `sidebar.shown_dir()`, a new `Ask::Tap((_, Tap::Close(i)))` case passes `sidebar.dir(i)`; answer `Routed::Watch(None, ..)` only when the shown workspace closed, else `Routed::Answer(Step::Draw(..))`. window.rs is 495 lines: keep it net-zero (the lit-target code in `view` already lights a sidebar target; check the ✕ lights alone).

Tests (behaviour). scene/sidebar/tests/close.rs (tests.rs is 454 lines): each workspace has exactly one Close target, inside its name line, at least 28 pt wide, listed before its row target; none when collapsed or with no list; `dir` past the end is None; `closed` of a row that is not shown keeps the shown one; `closed` of the shown one shows the first usable. crates/app/src/tests/close.rs (add only `mod close;` to tests.rs, 459 lines) against a real daemon with two workspaces open: a press and lift on the other row's ✕ closes it in the daemon (workspace_list), answers Routed::Answer, and the shown workspace is unchanged; the same on the shown row answers Routed::Watch(None, _); with no daemon on the socket the row stays and the flash says why.

Docs: ARCHITECTURE.md (window.rs, scene/sidebar.rs and scene/taps.rs paragraphs), CHANGELOG.md under Unreleased. docs/hand-check.md, one line: in the bundle, the ✕ on a row closes that workspace without switching, with the pen and the mouse; the ✕ does not crowd a long name; closing the shown one shows another; opt+cmd+W still works.

Not here: stopping the agent of a closed workspace (slinger-0f6923), a recent list, sidebar scrolling (slinger-d85d5a).

steps.title: app: one pure enabled predicate; menu bar items grey out when their command cannot act
steps.description:
Goal: one pure function says whether a command can act now, and the menu bar greys the items it says no to. Later steps reuse it for context menus.

Files. New crates/app/src/commands/able.rs (pure, no scene types): `pub struct Facts` and `pub fn can(command: Command, facts: &Facts) -> bool` as one exhaustive match with no `_` arm, so a new command must decide. Facts holds only what the rules read, for example: how many panes; whether the focused pane shows a canvas or an agent UI; how many items are selected there and whether one is a box; whether a box can be stepped into (canvases.step_target) and whether the pane is stepped in; how many pages; whether a find is active; whether a workspace shows and whether its agent exists and runs; whether a notice shows. commands/menu.rs: `Item` gains `pub enabled: bool`; `bar(keys, checked, facts)` sets it from `can` (a native item stays true: the window validates cut, copy and paste through Event::Can as today); add `pub fn same_layout(a: &[Menu], b: &[Menu]) -> bool`, true when two bars differ only in `enabled`. New crates/app/src/window/facts.rs: `pub fn facts(shared, canvases, sidebar, area) -> Facts` from existing queries; a missing read-only accessor goes in the canvases/ file that owns that state (canvases.rs is 497 lines: add nothing there). window.rs `view` passes the facts to `bar`; window.rs is 495 lines, so move a self-contained part out if needed (for example `finder` and `export_ui` to window/files.rs). platform/menu.rs: `Target` answers `validateMenuItem:` with the `enabled` of the item with that tag in the newest model (the MADE thread-local); `show` keeps the NSMenu and only stores the new model when `same_layout` holds, and rebuilds otherwise as now.

The rule for `can`: false only where `window::run` for that command would now do nothing or only flash a refusal; when unsure, true. Read each command's code before deciding. Starting list to verify: ClosePane, GrowPane, ShrinkPane and the Focus commands need more than one pane; ExportUi needs an agent UI pane; DeleteSelection, Duplicate and the Nudges need a selection; ClearSelection needs a selection or a stepped-in pane (it steps out); Fold needs a selected box; StepIn and StepInBeside need a step target; StepOut needs a stepped-in pane; NextPage, PreviousPage and RemovePage need a second page; FindNext needs a find; CloseWorkspace and ShowWorkspaceFolder need a shown workspace; StartAgent needs an agent that does not run, StopAgent one that runs, RestartAgent an agent; DismissNotice needs a notice. Undo and Redo stay on (the app does not know the daemon's undo stack). Sling stays on for a canvas pane (with nothing selected it slings what is new).

Keys do not change: AppKit does not fire a disabled item for its key, so the key reaches the keymap and the command answers as before. Say so in the module doc of commands/menu.rs and in ARCHITECTURE.md's Keys section.

Tests. commands/able tests: one case per rule, both ways. commands/menu/tests.rs: `bar` greys what `can` refuses; natives stay enabled; `same_layout` is true for an enabled-only change and false for a title, key, check or order change; the existing tests still pass with a Facts in which everything can act. crates/app/src/tests/able.rs with the World and a real daemon: for several states (nothing selected, one pane, one page, a canvas pane) every command `can` refuses is run through route() and changes nothing (item count, pane count, page count); and a command it allows (delete with a selection) acts. A key for a refused command still answers as before.

Docs: ARCHITECTURE.md (commands.rs, window.rs, platform/menu.rs), CHANGELOG.md. docs/hand-check.md, one line: in the bundle, open each menu with and without a selection, on an agent UI pane, with one pane and one page: the right items are grey and none is grey that would work; a greyed item's key still flashes why; Cut, Copy and Paste still grey as before; an item's state is right the moment the menu opens.

steps.title: app: the standard Mac menus: Hide, Hide Others, Show All, Services, Full Screen, Zoom, Window, Help
steps.description:
Goal: the app menu and the Window menu hold what every Mac app has, and AppKit knows which menu is Window, Services and Help.

Files. commands/menu.rs (pure): `Action::Separator`; `Native` adds Hide, HideOthers, ShowAll, Services, FullScreen, Zoom and BringAllToFront with their titles ('Hide slinger', 'Hide Others', 'Show All', 'Services', 'Enter Full Screen', 'Zoom', 'Bring All to Front') and usual keys (cmd+H, opt+cmd+H, ctrl+cmd+F; none for the rest), each key shown only while the keymap does not bind that chord, as Cut's is today; `Menu` gains `pub role: Role` (App, Plain, Window, Help). Lay out: slinger = About slinger, separator, Reload config, separator, Services, separator, Hide slinger, Hide Others, Show All, separator, Quit slinger. Window = Minimize, Zoom, Enter Full Screen, separator, Show or hide sidebar, Dismiss notice, separator, Bring All to Front. The other menus keep their items and order. commands/registry.rs: Quit's title becomes 'Quit slinger'; the native 'Minimise' becomes 'Minimize' (macOS's own names for its own items; other titles are not touched). platform/menu.rs: a separator is NSMenuItem::separatorItem; Services is an item with an empty submenu handed to NSApplication::setServicesMenu; a menu with Role::Window goes to setWindowsMenu and Role::Help to setHelpMenu; selectors hide:, hideOtherApplications:, unhideAllApplications:, toggleFullScreen:, performZoom:, arrangeInFront:, all sent along the responder chain like the existing natives. Platform reads only the role and the action, never a title. Check platform/panel.rs, which swaps the bar for a bare Edit menu while a panel is up and puts it back: the Window and Services registrations must hold after it. config.example.toml: one comment line that cmd+H, opt+cmd+H and ctrl+cmd+F are macOS's while no command is bound to them.

Do not add a Settings item: slinger-54ae6e adds the command; its place is after About.

Tests (commands/menu/tests.rs): the menu order test is unchanged; every command is still in exactly one menu; the app menu's and the Window menu's items in order; no menu starts or ends with a separator or has two in a row; Hide loses its key when the keymap binds cmd+H; no two items answer to one key; exactly one menu has each of the App, Window and Help roles. If step 2 has landed, `same_layout` treats a separator like any item.
