steps.title: app: right and middle button events reach the app; a pure module tells a context click from a pan
steps.description:
Goal: the decision 'click or drag' for the right button moves out of platform into a tested pure module. A right drag and a middle drag pan as before. A right click (and a ctrl+click, a two-finger trackpad click, a tablet button set to right click) no longer pans by its jitter; it focuses the pane under it. Step 5 makes it open a menu.

Files. platform/mod.rs is 498 lines: first move `Event` and `Step` into a new platform/event.rs and re-export them (a pure move; main.rs keeps importing them from crate::platform). New pure crates/app/src/scene/secondary.rs: `Button {Secondary, Middle}`, `Phase {Down, Drag, Up}` and a `Secondary` state with `down(button, at)`, `drag(at) -> Option<(Point, f64, f64)>` (the press point and the delta to pan by; None until the pointer is more than SLOP, 4 pt, from the press, then the whole way so far, so the canvas does not lag the pointer) and `up(at) -> Option<Point>` (the press point when a Secondary press never passed the slop: a context click; never for Middle; None with no press). Model it on scene/hand.rs. Keep it in Shared beside `hand`. platform/event.rs: `Event::Button { button, phase, at }`. platform/input.rs: RightMouseDown/Dragged/Up and OtherMouse* with button 2 dispatch Event::Button and return what dispatch returns; the RIGHT cell goes. A LeftMouseDown with control held is sent as Secondary Down, and the LeftMouseDragged and LeftMouseUp after it as Secondary Drag and Up (one Cell<bool> is the only state): macOS defines ctrl+click as the secondary click. Update the module docs of input.rs and platform/mod.rs. route.rs: handle Event::Button before `asked`, as `hand` is: Down is taken (Step::Stay) except over an open entry field (canvases.sling_covers(at), and the feedback and rename entries if they have a field there), where it is Step::Pass so the native text menu shows; Drag pans through window::gesture with Event::Scroll { at: press point, dx, dy } exactly as the platform's scroll did (over a pane that is not a canvas it passes, as today); Up with a click moves the pointer (tools.moved), focuses the pane under it as a press does (Shared::press_focus) and draws; under the key overlay, the palette, the page menu or an open tool pop-up it does nothing.

Consequence to state in the CHANGELOG: because the app takes the right press, WebKit's own menu (Reload, Back) no longer opens over an agent UI pane or a live item.

Tests. scene/secondary/tests.rs: a lift inside the slop is a click at the press point; a drag past the slop pans by the whole movement and the lift is then no click; coming back inside the slop after leaving it is still a pan; the middle button pans and never clicks; an up or a drag with no down is nothing; a second down replaces the first. crates/app/src/tests/secondary.rs with the World and a real daemon: a Secondary down, drags and up move the viewport as the same Event::Scroll deltas do; a click leaves the viewport and the canvas unchanged and focuses the pane under it; a Down over the open sling entry passes; a middle drag pans.

Docs: ARCHITECTURE.md (platform/ paragraph, route and shared), docs/design/pen-less.md (the right button: drag pans, click is the context click; a tablet button set to right click does the same), CHANGELOG.md. docs/hand-check.md, one line: in the bundle and on real hardware, right drag and middle drag pan as before with a mouse; a two-finger trackpad click and a ctrl+click pan nothing; ctrl+drag pans; a Wacom side switch set to right click acts as a right button; the sling entry's field still shows the system text menu on a right click; an agent UI no longer shows WebKit's menu.

steps.title: app: a context click pops a native menu for a pane, a footer or the empty canvas
steps.description:
Goal: the first whole slice: a context click (step 4) on the empty part of a canvas, on a pane's footer or on an agent UI pane opens an NSMenu whose items come from a pure function; a pick runs the command on the pane the click focused.

Files. New pure crates/app/src/commands/context.rs: `pub enum Subject { Canvas { stepped: bool }, Pane { ui: bool } }` (later steps add variants), `pub struct Popup { pub at: Point, pub items: Vec<Item> }` and `pub fn items(subject: &Subject, keys: &Keymap, checked: Command, facts: &Facts) -> Vec<Item>`. It builds each Item as `bar` does (share that one constructor in commands/menu.rs): title from Command::title, key from the live keymap (not one that types), `enabled` from able::can, separators as Action::Separator. Menus: Canvas = Paste (native), New text, Select all, separator, Sling now, separator, Zoom to 100%, Dotted grid, separator, New page, Step out of box. Pane = Export agent UI… (only when `ui`), separator, Split right, Split down, Close pane. platform/event.rs: `Step::Menu(Popup, Box<Scene>)`. platform/mod.rs `dispatch`: draw the scene, then pop the menu, after the borrow of the answer is dropped (a pick dispatches a new event from inside the pop); `reply` treats it as a draw. platform/menu.rs: `pop(popup, view, mtm)` builds an NSMenu from the items with the existing `made()`, sets autoenablesItems off and each item's enabled from its Item (a native item in a popup is always enabled: a paste that goes nowhere flashes why, as its key does), and calls popUpMenuPositioningItem:atLocation:inView: at the point flipped to the view. Its command items go to the existing `run:`, so a pick arrives as Event::Command and acts on what the click made current. The timer fires while the menu is open (chrome::tick_after uses the common modes): the menu bar must not be rebuilt under it for an enabled-only change (step 2's same_layout). New crates/app/src/window/context.rs (window.rs is 495 lines): `subject_at(at, shared, canvases, area) -> Option<Subject>` from Panes::place and status::content: a footer or an agent UI pane is Pane, a canvas pane's content is Canvas { stepped } (later steps look for an item, a divider and the sidebar first). route.rs: the context click of step 4 now answers Step::Menu(Popup { at, items }, view) when there is a subject; tools.moved(at) has run, so 'New text' lands at the click.

Tests. commands/context tests: each subject's items in order; a rebound key shows on its item and a key that types does not; `enabled` follows `can` (Close pane is grey with one pane, Step out of box unless stepped in); no menu starts or ends with a separator or has two in a row; no command twice; 'Export agent UI…' only for an agent UI pane. crates/app/src/tests/context.rs with the World and a real daemon: a context click on the empty canvas answers Step::Menu with the Canvas items at that point; on a footer, and on an agent UI pane, the Pane items, and that pane has focus; under the open palette nothing; after the click Event::Command(Command::NewText) starts a text at the clicked point; Event::Command(Command::SplitRight) splits the clicked pane.

Docs: ARCHITECTURE.md (commands.rs, window.rs, platform/menu.rs, the Step list in platform/), CHANGELOG.md. docs/hand-check.md, one line: in the bundle, a right click, a ctrl+click and a two-finger click open the menu at the pointer on release, also on a second display and in full screen; a right drag still pans and opens nothing; each item runs; Escape and a click outside close it; an agent's change arriving while the menu is open does not close or break it.

steps.title: app: context menus for canvas items by kind, the selection and a text being typed
steps.description:
Goal: a context click on a canvas item opens a menu for that kind of item; on a selection, one for the selection. Finder's rule: a click on an item outside the selection selects it alone first; a click on a selected item, or inside the selection's box where a press would grab it, keeps the selection. The commands then act on the selection as they always do.

Files. New crates/app/src/canvases/context.rs (canvases.rs is 497 lines) with `impl Canvases`: `item_at(&self, panes, (pane, frame), at) -> Option<Hit>` where Hit says the item's kind (text, box and whether folded, arrow, stroke, pdf, live), and whether it is in the selection; and `select_only(&mut self, panes, pane, id)`. Reuse the select tool's own hit test (`topmost` in scene/select/pick.rs with REACH / zoom; make it pub(crate) rather than copy it) and canvases/live.rs `under` for a live item; honour the stepped-in view and folded boxes as a press does. Check in the code whether a live item and a pdf item can be selected, and leave out of their menus what cannot act. commands/context.rs: add `Subject::Item { kind }`, `Subject::Selection { count, has_box }` and `Subject::Typing` and their menus. Any item: Sling selection, separator, Cut, Copy (natives), Duplicate, Delete selection, separator, Pick a colour. A text adds Pick a text size, Bigger text, Smaller text. A box adds Fold or unfold box, Step into box, Step into box beside. A pdf adds Crop PDF and Show canvas file in Finder. A live item: Sling selection, Delete selection. Selection (more than one): Sling selection, separator, Cut, Copy, Duplicate, Delete selection, separator, Fold or unfold box (when it has a box), Pick a colour, Select nothing. Typing (a canvas text is being typed under the click): Cut, Copy, Paste only, and the text does not end. window/context.rs: `subject_at` looks for an item in a canvas pane before it answers Canvas, and the route selects per the rule before it builds the popup (the Facts must be read after the selection changed). Pick a colour and Pick a text size open their pop-up at the pointer, which the click already moved.

Tests. commands/context tests: each kind's items in order, the separator rules, Fold only with a box. canvases/context tests or crates/app/src/tests/context_items.rs with the World and a real daemon holding a text, an open box, a folded box and an arrow: a context click on the box selects it alone and answers the box menu; on one of two selected items it keeps both and answers the Selection menu; on an item while another is selected it selects the clicked one; then Event::Command(Command::DeleteSelection) deletes exactly the selection and Event::Command(Command::Fold) folds the clicked box; in a pane stepped into a box the click hits what the pane shows; a click on a text being typed answers the Typing menu and the text is still being typed.

Docs: ARCHITECTURE.md (canvases/context.rs, commands.rs), CHANGELOG.md. docs/hand-check.md, one line: in the bundle, right-click a stroke, a text, an open and a folded box, an arrow, a pdf page, a live item and a multi-selection: the clicked item is selected and each item does what it says; Cut, Copy and Paste from the menu work on items and inside a text being typed.

steps.title: app: context menus for sidebar workspace rows and pane dividers; a pick carries its subject
steps.description:
Goal: a context click on a workspace's rows in the sidebar offers Close workspace, Show workspace folder in Finder, Start agent, Stop agent and Restart agent for that workspace, whichever one the window shows, with no switch. A context click on a divider offers Grow pane and Shrink pane for that divider. A context click on the rest of the sidebar offers Open workspace… and Show or hide sidebar. These are the subjects that cannot be made current, so the pick carries its subject.

Files. commands/context.rs: add `Subject::Workspace { dir: PathBuf, .. }` (the folder names it, as workspace_close takes; never the row's index), `Subject::Divider { before: u32, ratio: f64 }` (the number of the pane before it, as pane_resize names it, and its split's share now) and `Subject::Sidebar`; `Popup` gains `pub subject: Subject`. Menus: Workspace = Close workspace, Show workspace folder in Finder, separator, Start agent, Stop agent, Restart agent in a new conversation; Divider = Grow pane, Shrink pane; Sidebar = Open workspace…, Show or hide sidebar. The Facts for a Workspace menu describe that row's workspace and agent, not the shown one's, so Start and Stop grey for it. platform/event.rs: `Event::Picked(Command, Subject)`. platform/menu.rs: a popup's command items get their own action (`pick:`), which dispatches Event::Picked with the popup's subject; the menu bar's `run:` is unchanged and still sends Event::Command. The app keeps no memory of the last popup. main.rs `ask` (473 lines; put new arms in window/context.rs if it would pass 500): Event::Picked closes what is open as Event::Command does, then asks `Ask::On(command, subject)`. route.rs and main's `asked`: for Subject::Workspace, CloseWorkspace goes to step 1's window::close_workspace with that folder; StartAgent, StopAgent and RestartAgent to window::agent, which now takes the folder (the key and the menu bar pass sidebar.shown_dir()); ShowWorkspaceFolder reveals that folder (window::finder takes it). For Subject::Divider, GrowPane and ShrinkPane move that divider by panes::STEP, held in the ratio's limits, locally (Panes::set_ratio) and at the daemon (Shared::resized), as a drag of it does. Any other subject or command runs as Ask::Run(command). window/context.rs `subject_at` order: the sidebar (a row is a Workspace; add `Sidebar::row_at(at, ..) -> Option<usize>` from the same layout its targets come from; elsewhere Sidebar), then a divider (Panes::divider_at), then a pane's item, canvas or footer. A click on step 1's ✕ target opens the row's menu too.

Tests. commands/context tests: the three menus; Start agent grey for a row whose agent runs and Stop grey for one that does not, whatever the shown workspace is. crates/app/src/tests/context_rows.rs with the World, the sidebar open and a real daemon with two workspaces: a context click on the row that is not shown answers Step::Menu with Subject::Workspace of its folder and does not change the shown workspace; Event::Picked(CloseWorkspace, that subject) closes that workspace in the daemon, answers Routed::Answer and leaves the shown one; Event::Picked(ShowWorkspaceFolder, ..) resolves that folder (test the pure part, window::finder); a context click with no pick followed by Event::Command(Command::CloseWorkspace) closes the shown workspace, not the clicked one; a context click on a divider answers Subject::Divider and Event::Picked(GrowPane, ..) moves that divider's share by one step and no other divider.

Docs: ARCHITECTURE.md (the command path: Event::Command against Event::Picked; window.rs, platform/menu.rs), CHANGELOG.md. docs/hand-check.md, one line: in the bundle, right-click a workspace that is not shown: Close closes it and the window does not switch; Start, Stop and Restart act on that row's agent and the flash names it; Show folder opens its folder; right-click a divider and grow and shrink it; right-click the empty sidebar and open a workspace.

risks: Timing of a popup pick: popUpMenuPositioningItem runs its own tracking loop inside dispatch. The answer's borrow must be dropped before the pop, or the pick is dropped by try_borrow_mut. Only a hand check proves it.

The timer fires while a menu is open (common run-loop modes). A menu bar rebuilt under an open menu, or a scene drawn under a popup, may close or corrupt it; step 2's same_layout guards the bar, the hand check in step 5 covers the popup.

Taking the right press at sendEvent: is assumed to stop WebKit's menu over an agent UI, and passing it over an entry field is assumed to keep the native text menu. Neither can be tested without the bundle.

After a ctrl+click or a popup, AppKit may swallow the mouse-up. The pure Secondary state must not stay 'pressed': a new down replaces the old one (tested), and a Lift with no Press must stay harmless.

can() may grey a command that would have worked; the user then has only the key. The rule is 'false only when provably a no-op', the match is exhaustive, and step 2's route-level test runs every refused command.
platform code is not covered by tests and the workspace floor is 86%: a step that puts logic in platform can fail check:coverage. Keep platform to translation.
Several files are at the 500-line cap; a step that forgets to split first fails check:size late.

The close mark makes closing one tap, with no confirm and no undo (the workspace reopens with shift+cmd+O). Until slinger-0f6923 lands, closing a workspace whose agent runs leaves that agent with nothing to stop it.

Until slinger-eaa98b lands, the sidebar can show workspace B for up to a second while the panes are still A's. Steps 1 and 7 name workspaces by folder, so they do not add to it, but the menu-bar close still acts on what the sidebar says is shown.
The steps touch the same few files (commands/menu.rs, platform/menu.rs, route.rs, window/context.rs). Run them in order, one at a time, or expect merge conflicts.
sd keeps a step's `description` only in the plan row (sd plan show --json); a child seed's own description is just the back-reference. Whoever delegates must hand the step's description to the agent.
acceptance: A right click, a ctrl+click and a two-finger trackpad click on a sidebar workspace row, a canvas item, a selection, the empty canvas, a pane's footer, an agent UI pane and a divider each open a native menu on release; a right drag and a middle drag still pan and open nothing.
Every context menu item is a registry command or a native edit item, shows the command's title and live key, and is grey when commands::able::can refuses it; the menu bar greys by the same function.
A workspace that the window does not show can be closed, and its agent started or stopped, from its sidebar row, by the ✕ and by the context menu, and the window keeps showing what it showed.
A failed close leaves the row in the sidebar and says why; a menu dismissed without a pick changes what no later command acts on.
close-workspace is still on opt+cmd+W; no default key changed.

The app menu has Hide slinger (cmd+H), Hide Others, Show All, Services and Quit slinger; the Window menu has Minimize, Zoom, Enter Full Screen (ctrl+cmd+F) and Bring All to Front; AppKit knows the Window, Services and Help menus.

crates/app/src/platform holds no decision about what a menu contains, whether an item is enabled, or whether a press was a click: commands/able.rs, commands/context.rs and scene/secondary.rs do, each with unit tests.
No .rs file is over 500 lines, budgets/ is unchanged or tighter, and cargo xtask check-all is green after every step.
docs/hand-check.md has one line per step for what only the owner can check in the bundle; ARCHITECTURE.md and CHANGELOG.md describe each change in the commit that made it.

name: Command targets: context menus, sidebar close, standard Mac menus

sections.context: Every canvas lives at canvases/<id>.canvas in the daemon's data directory, while its workspace's slinger-workspace.toml sits in the user's folder (seed slinger-7c18bc, audit of 2026-11-20). Syncing the folder (2 of the owner's 3 open workspaces are under ~/sync) moves only the toml, and opening that folder on another machine silently makes an empty canvas of the same id (workspaces.rs open ignores the conflict from canvases.create). PDF and live-UI blobs are only in this machine's record.sqlite (O8), so a copied canvas loses them. Read from the code for the design: the daemon holds each canvas file open for its whole life and never looks at the path again, so a sync client that replaces the file leaves the daemon appending to an unlinked inode (acknowledged changes lost); and once canvases live in folders, two daemons with different data directories (the owner's and a test's) can open the same file. Owner decision (2026-11-20, not reopened): canvases become visible files in the workspace folder, with their blobs alongside; a design doc first. The design is docs/design/storage.md (picks in its 'Recommended' section, owner to confirm); its measurements are in docs/perf/canvas.md and its own table (a 28.9 MB canvas copies, syncs and hashes in about 50 ms; opening it to check costs 596 ms; a stat before each append costs 1-2 us against a 5 ms append).
sections.approach:
Guard first, then teach the daemon to follow a canvas that is elsewhere, then carry blobs, then stop for the owner, then move one canvas by hand, then make new and synced folders use folder canvases, and only last move the rest automatically. Each step is one gated commit that leaves main working, and nothing moves an existing canvas before the owner-review step.

1. Writer guard (storage.md Q4 A): flock(LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB) on each canvas file the daemon holds; a second daemon gets the canvas read-only and every change is conflict with a hint. Before each append, stat the path and compare device, inode, size and mtime with what the daemon last wrote; on a difference save the bytes the daemon holds beside the file as '<id> (slinger <machine> <time>).canvas', reopen the new file, refuse the change with conflict, and say so on stderr. Lands while canvases are still in the data directory, so it is pure safety.
2. Links (Q2 A): the core owns a link header {"slinger":"canvas","v":2,"id":..,"at":<absolute path>} in canvas::file (parse and write). Canvases::path is the only place that follows one; canvas_list lists linked canvases; canvas_show.path is the real file. Nothing writes links yet, so tests craft them.
3. Blobs (Q3 A): for a canvas whose file is outside the data directory, every change that names a blob (pdf or live hash in add, restore, set) writes the blob to <dir>/.slinger/blobs/sha256-<hex> (write once, temp and rename); a blob missing from the record is read from there and stored. UI catalog stays in the record (D19).
4. Owner review of storage.md's picks: the one owner-review step; it blocks everything that writes into a user folder or moves a canvas.
5. canvas_move verb (Q5 A): 'slinger canvas move <ID>' moves one canvas into its workspace's folder with the four-step move in storage.md (copy, check by hash and Log::open, hard-link the original into canvases/moved/, rename the link over canvases/<id>.canvas); '--back' copies the folder file's current bytes back over the link. Refuses a network file system (Q7 A) and a folder that already holds other bytes. Core, control, daemon, CLI, in that order, per 'Adding a verb'.
6. New and synced folders (Q6 A): workspace_open of a folder makes the canvas in the folder (with a link), and a folder that already holds <canvas>.canvas is adopted instead of making an empty twin; a header-only twin goes to moved/, a twin with content stays and the workspace is listed with a problem naming both paths.
7. Automatic move on start: the daemon moves each open workspace's canvases (its canvas and its layout's canvas: panes, named by no other open workspace) into the folder, using step 5's move; 'slinger canvas move --back --all' undoes it. Then scripts/perf-canvas.py is run again with the canvas in a folder.

Why this shape: the guard closes a hole that moving would widen, so it goes first; the link makes an older slingerd refuse a moved canvas (canvas_too_new, checked in read_header) rather than make a twin, so a mixed fleet never forks silently; blobs land before any move so a moved canvas never loses a PDF; the explicit move lets the owner rehearse on one canvas and roll back with one command or one cp, because the format does not change.

alternatives.name: Move every canvas automatically on the first start of the new build
alternatives.rejected_because: No rehearsal on the owner's real canvases, which are 10-15x anything measured here and cannot be copied for testing. The explicit move (step 5) is the rehearsal; the automatic move (step 7) reuses its code.

alternatives.name: An index file (canvases/index.json, id to path) instead of link headers
alternatives.rejected_because: An older slingerd ignores it, finds no file for a moved id, and workspace_open makes an empty twin: the bug this seed is about, now across builds. A link in the canvas's own place makes an old build refuse with canvas_too_new.

alternatives.name: Derive the path from the open workspaces, with no index at all
alternatives.rejected_because: A closed workspace's canvas becomes unreachable by id, a folder moved in Finder loses its canvas with no trace, and an older build makes the twin.

alternatives.name: A lock file .<id>.canvas.lock with machine and pid in the folder (the seed's direction)
alternatives.rejected_because: It syncs, goes stale when a machine dies, and adds a file to the user's folder and its sync conflicts. flock covers this machine (K5's scope); the stat check catches another machine's write arriving through the sync.

alternatives.name: Embed blobs in the canvas log
alternatives.rejected_because: Multi-MB base64 lines in a text log break grep and jq, and every replay and compaction carries them.

alternatives.name: Write to the data directory and copy to the folder in the background
alternatives.rejected_because: An acknowledged change would not be where the user sees it, and two copies must be kept in step.

alternatives.name: Move loose and rootless canvases to ~/Documents/Slinger in this plan
alternatives.rejected_because: Not needed for the bug, and a second new location to support and roll back. Left to the owner (docs/open-picks.md).

steps.title: daemon: flock each canvas file and refuse an append after an outside change
core, daemon: follow a canvas link header (v2 with 'at') to a canvas outside the data dir
daemon: write the blobs a folder canvas names to <dir>/.slinger/blobs and read them back
owner review: confirm the picks in docs/design/storage.md before any canvas moves
core, control, daemon, CLI: canvas_move moves one canvas into its folder and back
daemon: a new folder workspace's canvas lives in the folder; a synced canvas is adopted
daemon: move open workspaces' canvases into their folders on start; move --back --all

risks: The owner's real canvases are 10-15x the largest measured (scale 5, 28.9 MB) and were never seen. The move is linear in size (copy and hash about 50 ms, the Log::open check 596 ms at 28.9 MB), so a 60 MB canvas is about 1.3 s per move at start; step 7 moves canvases one at a time before the socket serves, which delays the first reply by that much. If that is too slow, move after serving, canvas by canvas, under each canvas's lock.

An fsync on a synced or network disk was not measured (no such disk here; the owner's ~/sync is private). The pick keeps network file systems out (statfs type); a local folder that a sync client reads is assumed to sync as fast as the data directory. Re-run scripts/perf-canvas.py with the canvas in a folder in step 7.

A sync client replacing the file while the daemon holds it is caught by step 1 only at the next append; a canvas that is only read keeps serving the old content until then. Acceptable for v1 (K5); a file watcher is later work.
Link headers spend canvas header version 2. A future real format change must use 3, and docs/design/canvas-file.md must say so in step 2.
flock is per machine and advisory: another program (an editor, git) ignores it. Step 1's stat check is what catches those, after the fact, keeping both copies.

Two workspaces with the same name in two folders still collide on the global canvas id (seed finding 'global namespace'); with canvases in folders the second one now fails loudly at open (conflict on the link) rather than sharing. Scoped ids are not in this plan.
Compaction (not in this plan) rewrites a file by rename, which step 1 reads as an outside change unless compaction updates the identity under the same lock. Note it where compaction is designed.

Repos opened as workspaces (this repo is one on the owner's machine) gain an untracked <id>.canvas and .slinger/ beside the toml. The user decides to commit or ignore them; slinger does not edit .gitignore.

Files near the 500-line cap: daemon canvases.rs 423, store.rs 489, workspaces.rs 493, server.rs 482, control lib.rs 487. Step 1 and step 5 put new code in new modules (canvases/guard.rs, canvases/moving.rs, control move.rs), not in those files.

sd spawns each child seed from the step's title, type, priority, labels and blocks only: point each worker at docs/design/storage.md ('Recommended' and the question its step builds) and at this plan's approach item with the same number.
acceptance: With a canvas open in one test daemon, a second daemon on another data directory that opens the same file gets conflict on every change, with a hint naming the file (test).

Replacing a held canvas file by rename (as a sync client does) makes the next change fail with conflict; the bytes the daemon held are saved beside the file and the new file is what the canvas shows next; no acknowledged line is lost (test).

A canvas whose canvases/<id>.canvas is a link header is shown, listed, changed and read through its id exactly as before, canvas_show.path names the folder file, and a build from before step 2 opening that link fails with canvas_too_new and writes nothing (test with the core's reader at v1).
A PDF canvas moved to a folder and opened by a daemon with an empty record shows its PDF pages (blob read from <dir>/.slinger/blobs).

slinger canvas move <ID> then slinger canvas move --back <ID> leaves canvases/<id>.canvas byte-identical to the folder file at the moment of --back, and canvases/moved/<id>.canvas byte-identical to the original before the move; a crash simulated after each of the four move steps leaves a canvas that opens with every acknowledged line (tests).

Opening a folder that holds main.canvas on a fresh data directory shows that canvas, not an empty one; opening it where the data directory has a twin with content keeps the twin, lists the workspace with a problem naming both paths, and loses neither (tests).
A folder on a network file system keeps its canvas in the data directory, with a problem line (test through a stubbed statfs type).

After step 7 the owner's open workspaces' canvases are in their folders, each original is in canvases/moved/, and slinger canvas move --back --all restores the data-directory layout an older slingerd reads (hand check on the owner's machine, docs/hand-check.md).
